terms.basis: The book's reporting basis. Automatic journals currently follow actual payments, regardless of this label.
terms.primary: The book that receives automatic payment and transfer journals. Keep exactly one active book marked as primary.
terms.header: A group that organizes other accounts. It cannot receive journal lines itself.
terms.posting: Posting accounts receive debit and credit lines. Header accounts only group other accounts.
terms.section: Where the account belongs in financial reports: assets, liabilities, equity, income, or expenses.
terms.normalBalance: The side on which this account usually has a balance. It does not mean money coming in or going out.
terms.bankControl: The ledger account representing a bank balance. A bank connection links an operational bank to this account.
terms.manualPosting: Whether this account is intended for journal lines entered directly by an accountant, rather than generated from payments.
terms.debit: One side of an accounting entry. Debiting a bank account increases it; for an outgoing payment, the category's debit account is the other side.
terms.credit: The other side of an accounting entry. Crediting a bank account reduces it; for a receipt, the category's credit account records the counterpart.
terms.policy: A rule connecting a cashflow category to accounting accounts in a particular book.
terms.clearing: An intermediate account used while a transaction is being completed. This setting is not used by the current automatic payment flow.
terms.accrual: Recognizing income or expenses when earned or incurred, even before payment. These account settings are not used by current automatic settlement journals.
terms.postingDate: The date on which an entry affects accounting records. For automatic payment journals, this is the payment's value date.

setupFlow.activationConsequences: Activation enables future postings. It does not import historical transactions, create opening balances, or change existing journals.
setupFlow.optionalGuidance: Periods and opening balances are optional. Bank connections and category rules are required only for the transactions that use them.
setupFlow.validationSource: Progress is validated against your saved configuration.
setupFlow.notActive: Finish setup before creating accounting entries.
setupFlow.attention: Configuration needs attention. Posting is blocked until the required settings are valid again.
setupFlow.blockedDescription: Review the pending prerequisites below, then return to this step. Your saved configuration is preserved.
setupFlow.actionError: The change could not be saved. Review the details and try again.
setupFlow.requestAdmin: An administrator with accounting configuration permission must activate this workspace.
setupFlow.profileGuidance: Choose a personal or organizational starting point. Templates are generic, not jurisdiction-specific accounting frameworks. Review the chart and book basis for your reporting needs.
setupFlow.afterBooks: Available after chart and book validation
setupFlow.periodGuidance: Optional date controls for each book. Without periods, posting remains date-based. Once periods exist, every posting date must fall in one open period.
setupFlow.bankGuidance: Map each bank used for receipts, payments, or transfers to an active bank-control posting account.
setupFlow.policyGuidance: Choose the debit and credit accounts for categories used in actual receipts and payments. Unused categories do not block setup.
setupFlow.openingGuidance: If opening balances are needed, record a balanced manual journal after activation. Activation never creates balances automatically.
setupFlow.noPeriods: No periods configured. Dates remain unrestricted until periods are defined.
setupFlow.periodConsequences: Soft-closing or closing blocks new postings, including corrections. Reopen before posting. Period dates can be corrected until the period is used in a journal.
